profile.reading:
DataBank EWR2 sits at 25 Corporate Place South, Piscataway, New Jersey, in Middlesex County within the New York metro's New Jersey data center corridor. DataBank's own facility page states 22,590 square feet of IT space and 3 megawatts of critical IT load, built to an N+1 power design DataBank describes as 100 percent renewable-sourced, with N+1 cooling supporting 10 kilowatt-plus rack densities, 9 onsite network carriers, and SOC 1/2, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, and ISO 27001:2022 compliance certifications. DataBank markets EWR2's connectivity through direct network links to major Manhattan and Newark carrier hotels, specifically citing 165 Halsey Street in Newark, 60 Hudson Street, and 111 Eighth Avenue in Manhattan, positioning EWR2 as a lower-cost, disaster-recovery-friendly alternative to New York City proper while retaining low-latency connectivity into the city's core interconnection points. DataBank separately operates EWR1 at 165 Halsey Street in Newark itself, a distinct 34,360 square foot, 1.7 megawatt facility not to be confused with this Piscataway site. DataBank does not publish a year-opened date, a formal Tier certification, or a named power utility for EWR2, and its New Jersey market pages do not reference any state-specific data center tax incentive, describing the market instead in general terms around proximity to New York City and the density of the regional carrier ecosystem.

New Jersey's data center corridor, including Piscataway, Newark, Weehawken, and Secaucus, has developed as a lower-cost alternative to Manhattan proper while retaining direct fiber connectivity into the city's core carrier hotels, a positioning DataBank's own EWR2 marketing leans on explicitly. Middlesex County's office and light-industrial parks along the New Jersey Turnpike corridor have hosted telecommunications and data infrastructure tenants for decades, predating the more recent wave of hyperscale campus development that has concentrated further west and south in New Jersey and Pennsylvania.
